entities.summary: Pierpaolo Parisio (1473–1545) was an Italian bishop and Cardinal. As a prelate of the Catholic Church, Parisio played a significant role in the Renaissance humanist movement. He was a strong advocate for the Catholic faith and served as a diplomat between the Holy See and European monarchs. Parisio's career was marked by controversy, as he was accused of simony and heresy. Despite these challenges, he remained a prominent figure in Italian Catholicism until his death in 1545. The legacy of Pierpaolo Parisio can be seen in the many Catholic institutions and charities he established during his lifetime. His commitment to the Catholic faith and his role in shaping the Renaissance humanist movement continue to be studied by scholars today.
